comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED and PUSHED as Gerrit 1903, Change-Id I3f5e57df. Rebased onto origin/main 74517a190e (RP-04 C3g) first, cleanly. binding_recovery.py 411 -> 466; binding_store.py 530 -> 552; reconcile.py 795 -> 799, exactly the four-line budget.

THE PLANNED INVOCATION SITE WAS WRONG AND WAS CORRECTED BEFORE THE ATTESTATION. Both the story and this task named run_differs.py; nothing inside it can satisfy the ordering, because reconcile._load_snapshots constructs the store, runs the under-lock staleness gate and performs the FIRST remote fetch all within one call, while bind_operation_runtime and run_differs both run after that call returns. The epic's "after the configuration snapshot AND before the remote fetch" is an EMPTY window for the same reason. Completion reads only local binding state, so the snapshot conjunct was dropped rather than satisfied and the pre-observation half kept. reconcile.py is the site; run_differs.py is untouched. The coordinator independently verified all of this against origin/main.

THE REAL CONSTRAINT WAS NEVER run_differs.py's 61 LINES — it is reconcile.py's FIVE (795/800). The spine got 4 lines (one call, three comment) and the entire guard lives in binding_recovery.py.

FOUR LINES ADDED TO THE SPINE, placed after the sync_pass_start log and before the fetch:
    # Interrupted-retirement repair (RP-02 S3 T2): after the under-lock staleness gate,
    # and BEFORE the first remote fetch below - so no pass can interleave fresh liveness
    # evidence for a retired issue with completing that issue's retirement.
    binding_store.repair_at_write_boundary(persist=persist, scoped=bool(scoped_ids))

GUARD SEMANTICS: refuses when `not persist or scoped`, and refusing is FREE - no classification, no repository read, no output. That matters because it is reached on every read-only command; a guard that classified and discarded would make the read-only path pay for a repair it is forbidden to perform. Refusal returns the same empty outcome type the admitted path returns, so no caller branches on "was I allowed".

OBSERVABILITY ADDED in response to the T5b advisory that recurred on both T1 and T2 rather than being deferred: completions and refusals each report one stderr line, and a healthy store reports NOTHING. A per-pass "nothing to repair" line would train operators to ignore the one line that matters, and a refusal is the finding that matters most since it is an inconsistent store that will not fix itself.

HELD-OUT TDD: 21 oracles RED-first against a signature-only scaffold (12 failed / 9 passed at RED; the 9 passed VACUOUSLY pre-wiring, which is why mutation mattered more than usual here). The implementer saw 10; 11 discriminators held outside the worktree and ALL passed unseen - both staleness-gate orderings, reconcile-check/selected/filtered refusals, the free-refusal proof, tombstone authority against a same-key confirm plus a cleared absence, explicit unretire, failure containment, and both reporting edges.

MUTATION KILLED ALL 7, and the one that matters most is N7: relocating the call to AFTER the first remote fetch is caught by two tests. That defect would leave the repair working, still tested, and silently wrong - and it is the realistic way this guarantee gets erased, because RP-03 S5 (diamond-flavoured-esok, postmodern-tangled-mollusk) is queued against reconcile.py and will have to extract from a file at the cap. Also killed: guard removed, operands swapped to AND, each condition dropped singly, classification hoisted above the guard, unconditional reporting. On the coordinator's advice the absence-only structural test became a POSITIVE plus negative anchor - it now asserts the call IS present in reconcile.py as well as absent from run_differs.py, with a docstring telling whoever extracts the file what must be preserved.

THREE TEST DEFECTS OF MINE, all found and reported by the implementer rather than worked around. (1) The ordering spy loaded binding_recovery.py under a fresh module name, building a DIFFERENT BindingRecovery class, so it patched a class nothing calls: the repair ran, no event was recorded, and the ordering assertion was UNFALSIFIABLE. Proven with SAME_CLASS False and with the RECON line appearing on stderr in the same run. Fixed to import the module production actually reaches. Galling detail: this file already carried a fixture docstring warning about exactly this hazard for the mode enum, and I then reproduced the hazard one fixture lower down. (2) and (3) Two pre-existing binding-store doubles needed the new method - _Bindings in test_bridge_selection_scope_heldout.py and FakeBindingStore in test_reconcile_filter.py - matching the maintenance test_reconcile_filter.py already documents for the acting-walk interface. A no-op is faithful there because neither double holds retired state. The implementer proved all five failures were test-side by applying the three edits temporarily, reaching the collection ceiling, then restoring byte-identically.

BASELINE CORRECTION: my stated 3373 was wrong - it was measured with held-out tests present. The visible-only ceiling for those two paths is 3362 + 9 skipped. Post-rebase with held-out restored: 3410 passed, 9 skipped.

SURFACE-PARITY CENSUS - ALL FIVE SLOTS IN SCOPE, not out, which is a change from T1. CLI: the reconciler's --mode and sync/preview routes are the only trigger. MCP: _mcp_reads exposes reconcile(mode) whose docstring promises reconcile-check and dry-run are non-mutating, so the persist half of the guard is what keeps that promise true of the new repair. Library facade: rebar.reconcile(mode) is exported from rebar/__init__. All three funnel through one mode -> MODE_CAPS -> persist derivation, so a single guard covers them uniformly. Automated callers: the load phase. Dual direction: unretire is the tested inverse.

RP-04 C3g INTERACTION CHECKED. C3g removed _env_int and the os import from binding_lifecycle.py and drained LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS to EMPTY (_ROWS = []). My oracles never patched binding_lifecycle.os or _env_int, and _DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE survives, so _make_overlap still drives note_absent to grace unchanged. Re-verified the three-miss plus 3600-second conjunction explicitly after the rebase: 4 passed. S3 adds NO ambient config read, so the newly-empty registry stays empty.

GATES: 3410 passed / 9 skipped (unit reconciler + interfaces/store + integration); 11728 passed / 53 skipped across the whole tests/unit tree pre-rebase; lint clean, mypy 567, complexity new=0 increased=0, comment hygiene, config ownership, env registry unchanged, reconcile.py 799/800.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
Construction-time or preview-time repair would violate read-only commands. Retirement completion is safe only after provider preflight and exclusive pass ownership succeed and under-lock staleness validation passes, and it must precede any remote observation so the pass cannot interleave fresh liveness evidence with completion.

## Outcome
Invoke the S3 recovery operation once at the validated write-bearing reconcile boundary before remote observation; every read-only or filtered path stays zero-write for this operation.

## Verified invocation site (corrected from this task's original impact set)
The original plan named `run_differs.py`. That is wrong, and the ordering it asked for is unreachable there. Verified by reading the spine:

- `reconcile._load_snapshots` is called at `reconcile.py:222`; inside it the binding store is constructed (`:280`), the under-lock staleness gate runs (`:281-282`), `scoped_ids` is computed (`:287`), and the FIRST remote issue fetch happens (`:328-333`).
- `bind_operation_runtime` (the immutable operation/config snapshot) is composed at `:227`, after `_load_snapshots` returns and therefore after that fetch.
- `run_differs()` is invoked at `:231`, also after the fetch; the existing `recover_pending_bindings` call at `run_differs.py:418` already runs post-fetch.

So the invocation goes in `reconcile.py`, after the staleness gate and the `scoped_ids` computation and before the fetch. `run_differs.py` is NOT edited by this task. The real size constraint is `reconcile.py` at 794 of the 800-line cap — SIX lines of headroom, and RP-04 S7.3.a is editing the same file — so the spine gets ONE call line plus a short comment, and no new import.

## Plan
1. Add `BindingRecovery.repair_at_write_boundary(*, persist, scoped)` owning the guard: it returns an empty outcome without any classification or write unless the pass is write-bearing (`persist`) and unscoped (`not scoped`). Expose it through the facade so the spine needs no new import. The unguarded `complete_interrupted_retirements()` from T1 keeps its semantics and stays the direct-test entry point.
2. Call it from `reconcile.py` on one line, positioned after the under-lock staleness validation and before the first remote issue fetch, binding walk, differ, or lifecycle mutation.
3. Treat a durable tombstone as authoritative until explicit `unretire`; an automatic 200, `clear_absent`, or same-key confirmation cannot revoke it.
4. On completion failure, preserve the overlap for retry. Because the call precedes the fetch, a failure structurally cannot have made a remote call.

## Testing
- Order tests pin the call between the staleness gate and the first fetch, and assert zero provider calls when completion aborts.
- A read-only table drives construction, load, reconcile-check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered paths and asserts zero repository writes attributable to this operation.
- Guard tests exercise `repair_at_write_boundary` directly across the persist/scoped matrix and prove the non-write-bearing cases do no classification at all.
- AC5 and AC6 are verified at the PASS level in `test_recovery_write_boundary.py`, not only at the owner level: one test drives a write-bearing pass over a historical overlap whose live record was reconfirmed to the same key and cleared of absence, and asserts the tombstone still completes and survives; a second lifts the tombstone with an explicit `unretire` first and asserts the pass leaves the live binding alone. The owner-level twins already exist from T1 in `state/test_binding_recovery.py` (`test_a_same_key_confirm_does_not_revoke_the_tombstone`, `test_clear_absent_does_not_revoke_the_tombstone`, `test_an_explicit_unretire_removes_the_completion_candidate`); the pass-level pair proves the guarded entry point does not lose that behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A live write-bearing unscoped pass completes exact recovery after the under-lock staleness gate.
- [x] That completion happens before the pass's first remote issue observation.
- [x] Construction, load, reconcile-check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered paths perform zero writes from this operation.
- [x] A completion failure performs zero remote calls and preserves the overlap as recoverable evidence.
- [x] An automatic success, absence reset, or same-key confirmation does not override the tombstone.
- [x] Explicit `unretire` removes the tombstone and therefore removes the completion candidate.
- [x] `run_differs.py` is unmodified and the pre-existing create-recovery gate is unchanged.

## Out of scope
Rich-emission caller cutover, ADR finalization, and any change to the pre-existing create-recovery gate (its no-write-pass remote-write defect is filed separately as `easygoing-tremendous-frogmouth`).

Single-line invocation after the under-lock staleness gate and before the first remote issue fetch.

Guard matrix, tombstone-authority, and failure-preservation regressions.
